text:
julia: Quick follow-up from the RFC thread — proposing a lightweight runtime gating layer for fused attention fastpaths so we can flip on/off without redeploying kernels.

nate: +1, we need that. currently switching kernels requires a full rollout and it's messy.

julia: Thinking of a predicate evaluated per-request (cheap) that picks: fused_qkv, fused_bias_rope, or dropout_free path. Example: 
```
if (seq_len <= 1024 && batch == 1 && !uses_dropout && rope_mode == 'standard') {
  path = 'fused_qkv_v3'
} else {
  path = 'compat'
}
```

tara: Love the idea but watch out for perf cliff when batch>1 or varying seq_len. we should collect histograms first.

raj: Agreed. Ops wants telemetry hooks: counts per path, p50/p95 latency, and unit cost delta. Also a fallback counter so we can auto-disable a path if errors spike.

mike: Implementation note: fused_bias_rope kernel currently assumes contiguous KV layout. if routing decides different layouts we'll need a cheap transform stage or we lose perf.

julia: Right — two options: 1) normalize layout in a tiny pre-step (cheap for small seqs), or 2) expand kernel signature to accept strides. Option 1 simpler to ship.

sophia: From model side, some evals show small output divergence for dropout-free inference vs train-time dropout averaged out. we need eval regressions flagged per-prompt set before changing default.

nate: Can we gate dropout-free path behind a model opt-in flag in model metadata? then rollout per-model.

julia: Yes — model manifest field `runtime.fastpaths = {"dropout_free": true}`. runtime checks that + predicate.

raj: Ops-bot idea: when a new fastpath flips on, emit a rollout event and create a short-lived alert rule: if error_rate > 0.5% or p99 latency > baseline*1.2 -> auto-revert.

ops-bot: deploy-check: rollout_event(created_by=julia, fastpath=dropout_free, scope=prod, id=fp-1845678901)

mike: Need an ABI compatibility test matrix: quantized int8 vs fp16 kernels, rope variant mixins, and bias/no-bias. If any combo fails, route to compat.

julia: Proposed runtime config schema fragment: 
```json
{"fastpath_predicates": [{"name":"short_seq_fused_qkv","seq_max":1024,"batch_max":4,"requires": ["no_dropout"]}]}
```

tara: Nice. Also add a safety TTL so a path can't remain enabled without telemetry for >24h; stale signal implies misconfig.

nate: For telemetry backend, we should sample 1/100 for full token-level profiling and aggregate counts for every request. that keeps cost low.

mike: Test plan: microbench kernel-only, end-to-end synthetic workloads, and a small canary traffic slice with golden prompts (from sophia).

sophia: I'll assemble prompt sets highlighting rope/bias sensitivity. include long-tail prompts too.

raj: Rollout steps checklist: 1) feature flag + manifest field, 2) telemetry hooks + dashboards, 3) canary 1% X 4h, 4) monitor regressions, 5) expand.

julia: I'll open the follow-up RFC PR with predicate API, schema, and a short reference impl in runtime. assign to mike/nate for kernel/telemetry work.

nate: Assigning to me and mike. we'll scope kernel changes to avoid broad ABI churn.

mike: I'll prototype layout-normalize pre-step and report back with perf numbers.

julia: Thanks all. any objections to me adding the ops-bot auto-revert rule to the RFC?

raj: No objections. strongly in favor.

tara: One more ask: add a deterministic unit test that toggles paths and asserts identical outputs (within tolerance) for a seed set.

julia: Will add. drafting RFC now, will ping when PR is ready. :rocket:
